word_cse shares a repeated load through its loads_mem facts, keyed by loadToNumList over Addr n2 offset. WordInst.mem carries no offset, so instruction selection leaves such a load as .assign dest (.load (.op .add [.var n2, .const offset])) until wordToStack fuses it, and CSE passed that carrier through untouched - reading one global twice emitted the global-table load twice where Cake emits it once.

Cake word_instScript.sml:234-245 and 252-275: only the outer constant displacement of a load address is held for Word-to-Stack fusion; a global base plus a computed offset uses the ordinary target selector so nested add/sub/shift immediates are preserved.

inst_select_exp c tar temp (Shift sh exp n) (word_instScript.sml) shifts the operand it selected, so a shift's left operand must not be discarded. With binary-operation immediates disabled for address selection that operand comes back as an expression, and ignoring it dropped the constant: lds 1 (1000 + (k - 1) * 8) compiled as lds 1 (1000 + k * 8). shifted_value is exact; shifted_offset and nested_shift now compute the right value but still cost two extra instructions, tracked by flapjack-cey.

inst_select_exp c tar temp (Load exp) (word_instScript.sml:234-245) splits on the address shape -- Op Add [exp'; Const w] keeps w for the Addr temp w displacement and selects only exp' -- and both recursive calls use the ordinary asm_config. Flapjack instead reconfigured the target with validBinOpImmediate := fun _ _ => false for the whole address, which also reached nested subexpressions: in lds 1 (table + (k - 1) * 8) the inner k - 1 came back as an expression rather than a register, so the Shift case could not use its immediate and materialized the shift amount into a second register. Cake emits addi/slli; Flapjack emitted ori/or/addi/sll. A global base is what exposes this, because a constant base normalizes to Op Add [shift; Const] and takes the displacement branch.

crep_to_loop$compile (Dec v e prog) (crep_to_loopScript.sml:409-415) extends the *incoming* live set for the body: fl = insert tmp () l, not the l' that compile_exp returned. compile_exp inserts its own temporaries (LoadByte, Load32, Cmp, Crepop) so that the code it emits can name them, but they are dead once the declared variable holds the value. Flapjack threaded the returned set instead, so every cutset inside a Dec body carried the initializer's temporaries: the Call cutset, the enclosing Loop entry set, and every If cutset. loop_live$shrink only intersects cutsets and a Loop whose Break restores the loop's entry set never shrinks below it, so the extra names survived to word_alloc and each one took a frame slot -- the cake_bitmaps frame word came out one to four powers of two too large, and the SSA copies of one value were given two different stack slots (a stack-to-stack move Cake does not emit). The four functions cover the four temporary-inserting compile_exp forms; main pins the whole-file layout.

inst_select_exp c tar temp (Op op [e1; Const w]) (word_instScript.sml:252-275) tests c.valid_imm (INL op) w for every operator; only the Sub retry with -w is Add-specific, and the remaining case materializes w into temp+1. Flapjack's expression-level selector tested the immediate for Add alone, so a nested x && 1w emitted ori t, x0, 1; and d, x, t where Cake emits andi d, x, 1 - one instruction more per occurrence. bit_test, or_immediate and xor_immediate cover the immediate path for And/Or/Xor; sub_immediate covers the Add/Sub retry; wide_mask and wide_or pin the no-immediate path, where the constant must still be materialized into temp+1 rather than left as an unfused expression - leaving it there makes the enclosing Shift miss its own immediate and cost two more instructions (guest bswap64, rmd_f).

word_simp$simp_duplicate_if (word_simpScript.sml:432-454) is structurally recursive and descends into Loop bodies, MustTerminate bodies and both sub-programs of a Call. Flapjack's executable version is fuel-driven and its wordProgFuel measure counted only Seq and If, so a whole while body was budgeted as one node and the recursion ran out of fuel part-way down it. A materialised comparison nested inside a loop body then kept its 0/1 round trip - bne; t := 0; jal; t := 1; beq t, 0 - where Cake folds the comparison straight into the branch: five instructions more per occurrence. break_then_more is the minimal shape (a comparison whose If is followed by further statements inside the loop); return_then_more is the guest's is_zero_bytes; nested_loop needs two levels of Loop descent; call_return_condition needs the Call return-program descent.

Reduced from the full stateless guest (15840 lines -> 3) by scripts/parity-reduce.py. Cake's word_to_stack$compile_prog computes stack_arg_count = arg_count - reg_count (word_to_stackScript.sml:587-593) with the reg_count word_to_stack$compile computes once for the whole program (line 605): asm_conf.reg_count - (5 + LENGTH asm_conf.avoid_regs), which for RISC-V is cakeRiscVRegisterCount = 22. PipelineDiagnostics used a literal 12, so every function with twelve or more word parameters reserved a frame Cake does not: eleven_words was exact while twelve_words and twelve_scalars each gained an addi sp, a stack-overflow check and a matching addi around a body that is one ori. Struct-vs-scalar is irrelevant; only the total word count matters, which is why the fixture pins eleven words, twelve words as two structs, and twelve scalars.

Reduced from the stateless guest's fp2_eq. Cake puts call argument i in colour i+1 (colour 0 is the link register) and every colour below k is a machine register, with k = asm_conf.reg_count - (5 + LENGTH asm_conf.avoid_regs) = 22 on RISC-V (word_to_stackScript.sml:605); the window in argument-index space is therefore k-1 = 21. WordStackConfig.abiRegisterCount defaulted to 12, the x10--x21 span, so a call with twelve or more word arguments was treated as having stack-resident arguments Cake keeps in registers: twelve_caller emitted an extra st x29, 24(x24) and freed three frame words where Cake frees four, and at fourteen or more arguments wordStackPhysicalMovesToIndexed returned none and the whole compile failed. ten_caller pins the arity just below the old threshold; twelve_caller pins the shape that used to differ.
Minimized full-guest secp256k1_recover call-frame witness; source-shaped Cake uses 22 stack-register ABI slots and StackArgs without a second argument-move pass.

Reduced from the stateless guest's g1_double by scripts/parity-reduce.py. Cake's word_to_stack keeps Addr base offset through a load exactly as it does through a store, and the Lab pass recognises the const/arith/memory triple for loads as well as stores, emitting memOffset. wordStackCompileLoadNatNested had no Addr base offset case: it always materialised the whole address into addressScratch, so a load whose destination is spilled came out as addi x23, base, off; ld scratch, 0(x23); sd scratch, slot(x24) against Cake's ld scratch, off(base); sd scratch, slot(x24). Only the spilled destination was affected, because a register destination fuses through the statement-level path; register_load pins that half as exact, spilled_load the half that differed. Guest sections g1_double, swu_g1, ecp_add and g1_add were this shape.

StackArgs dest arg_count (k,f,f') = stack_move n 0 f k (StackAlloc n) (word_to_stackScript.sml:287-292), and stack_move reads its source at start + f, where f is the caller's frame size from compile_prog -- f = if stack_var_count = 0 then 0 else stack_var_count + 1 -- not the public stack_var_count occupancy f'. Routing the pre-call overflow-argument copy through the allocator's own slot instead loads the wrong caller-frame word: the single wide_call_spilled_base witness had Cake loading 112(x24) where Flapjack loaded 56(x24). This fixture pins three overflow arities at once (24, 26 and 30 word arguments, so one, three and seven overflow slots) because the wrong slot is a function of f and a single arity cannot distinguish an off-by-one from a wrong formula. All three differ from Cake at 23eded92 and are byte-identical here.
